idiom_name: enum with named-field variants + exhaustive match
implementation_notes: Rust's syntax-tree crates are single enums whose variants carry named fields - syn's Expr::Binary { left, op, right }, and rustc follows the same design - so the irregular child list is expressed with the language's own sum type, and match gives node-specific traversal with compiler-enforced exhaustiveness instead of visitors or casts. Recursion is supplied by Box/Rc, and shared payloads (span, attributes) live in each variant or in a wrapper struct. This is the default realization; a class-style hierarchy only appears when downstream crates must extend the node set. Lossless/arena trees for editors are a different (normalized) family, not this pattern.
pitfalls: A recursive variant must indirect through Box or Rc - a variant containing the enum by value does not compile - and each Box costs an allocation, so deep trees are allocation-heavy.

Adding a variant is a breaking change for downstream matches unless the enum is #[non_exhaustive] and callers add a wildcard arm with the non_exhaustive_omitted_patterns lint (the idiom syn documents).
Ownership makes in-place rewriting awkward: passes usually rebuild subtrees functionally rather than mutate nodes.
